title: Dissolutions — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Dissolutions' rich face, at Sketch tier: one walk up to the seam in perception, made, and the rough it leads to, gathered, at the paragraph they test; and the six learning sequences, gathered beside the catalogue, each a way up that ends on its 2026-10-20 proof. Every section waits as a proposal until Loudon approves it. I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: 'Somewhere near 20 Hz' names one point where the hearing literature finds a zone between about 15 and 30 Hz. Loudness fluctuation gives way to roughness from about 15 Hz (Zwicker and Fastl, Psychoacoustics), and the lower limit of pitch is near 30 Hz (Krumbholz, Patterson and Pressnitzer 2000, JASA 108:1170; Pressnitzer, Patterson and Krumbholz 2001, JASA 109:2074). Proposed: 'somewhere between about 15 and 30 Hz it stops being heard as a change in loudness and starts being heard as a sound'. The maker first offered 20 to 30 Hz; the challenger's read of the same sources put the lower end at 15, and that read settled it. This comes from the literature, not a measurement, and the piece's blind glide lets a listener mark their own crossing.

pieces.title: One curve, read faster · a walk up to the seam
pieces.caption:
**Where does loudness become a sound, and who decides?** One curve, read out and back by one reader, goes out on two wires: one sets the loudness of a 220 Hz tone, the other sends the curve straight out. There are five steps: a fade you can count, the same fade faster, the straight wire alone, both wires together, and then the test, a 24-second glide from 4 to 64 Hz and back where you mark the change. The engine has no crossfade and no filter. Both levels stay the same at every speed, and it reports them at your mark. While the glide runs, the speed is hidden; it shows only at your mark, and the page's own number only after it. Use headphones: laptop speakers push the straight wire's seam far up.

y = A × f(t, c) × sin(2π × 220 × time) + B × (f(t, c) − m(c))

(what you hear) = (a fixed level) × (the curve's height at the reader) × (a 220 Hz tone) + (a fixed level) × ((the curve's height) − (its average))
pieces.near: A dissolution in the math can leave a seam in perception

pieces.title: One curve, three readers · the 2026-10-18 rough
pieces.caption: **The proof of the identity one line above: one curve, three readers.** This is the second rough from the 2026-10-18 Daily Page, played in its sit and gathered as it was. The gold curve stays put while the reader changes: an envelope, an oscillator, an effect. One thing to know first: this proof draws the seam in. Below 12 Hz it plays the curve only as a tone's loudness, above 30 Hz only as the sound itself, and it crossfades in between, so its line 'Crossing the seam' is the code's, not your ear's. On the seam the walk above is the stronger test: it keeps both wires open at fixed levels and leaves the seam to you.
pieces.near: A dissolution in the math can leave a seam in perception

verdicts.why: A real test with a clean walk up, but during the glide it shows the live reader speed and a meter that jumps from 31% to 100% at exactly 20 Hz, and step 5 names "near 20 Hz" first, so the mark is anchored to the page’s number. Blind the glide (hide speed, slider motion and meter while gliding; reveal the speed only in the marks table) and move "near 20 Hz" to after the first mark; the engine and its 9 PASS stay.

The played record of line 59’s identity, one curve with three readers; its crossfaded seam contradicts the paragraph, and the caption says so plainly. Note: it is the proof of the identity more than of the seam, which the walk’s own last step tests better; the caption could say so.

pieces.title: The table that travels · a way up to Dispersion Table
pieces.caption: **Is a wavetable a loop with its filter slot left empty?** Your outline from the sit, built out: the table alone, the loop alone, the two through their difference, the filter alone, the filter in the loop, and last the 2026-10-20 proof itself, unchanged. Every step has a notes box. On the last step, Send hands your notes to this section's note box below, and the face's Send takes them to the board.
pieces.near: the wavetable oscillator is the lossless waveguide loop

pieces.title: The shadow that locks · a way up to Phase Reduction
pieces.caption: **Why does the pitch climb as the coupling rises?** Your question from the sit, answered at step 5: the coupling is a spring, and locked nearly opposite, it stiffens every swing. The walk goes from one loop, through a kick and the curve it draws, to two loops joined, and ends on the proof. Notes as above: Send on the last step puts them in this section's box.
pieces.near: Kuramoto is the phase-reduced shadow of any population of limit cycles

pieces.title: The circle's shadow · a way up to Chebyshev is Fourier
pieces.caption: **How does one bent curve give back a whole stack of drawbars?** From a point going round a circle, to the stack, to one curve and the stack subtracted to silence, then what happens below full reach, and last the proof. The reach here runs 0.05 to 1, as the proof's does; the Chebyshev face's drive runs 1 to 1.30, so the two meet only at 1.
pieces.near: Chebyshev polynomials are Fourier basis under a coordinate change

pieces.title: One field, two hands · a way up to Volterra Kernels and the Torus
pieces.caption: **Is a synthesizer the same kernel as an effect?** One field, read by two phasors, then by its diagonal, then their difference, then the lag's test, the kernel, and the proof. Step 5 sets up offer A, held on the baton: a static curve does make difference tones, but only the lagged read makes a 30 Hz tone swing as two tones slide up together. The Volterra page says otherwise for now, and the sequence says so.
pieces.near: a synthesizer and an effect are the same kernel

pieces.title: The equation read backward · a way up to Linear Predictive Coding
pieces.caption: **Is analysis synthesis read backward?** A buzz and a mouth, a guess from one sample, then sixteen. What the guess misses is the residual, and running the line the other way gives the voice back. Then how many weights a vowel needs, and the proof.

pieces.title: The lattice read back · a way up to Rank-N Lattice Analysis
pieces.caption: **Does analysis recover the lattice synthesis used?** One generator, two, a ruler laid on the peaks, the bound, another basis, and the proof. It sets up offer B: rank means something only once the whole numbers are bounded, and the analysis returns the lattice, not the hand that drew it. Step 6 says why the proof's box puts √2 at whole numbers up to 157, where a search over every ruler fits from 65.
pieces.near: the minimal generating spectrum of a sound is the dual read
